items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The interviewee narrates facts about Jimmy Monroe's life and club ('Jimmy opened a club...', 'The club... became a big success') but does not state a personal interaction, relationship, or direct connection with Jimmy Monroe.

ctx.x: Fletcher had worked with Freddie Taylor and left to go to India with the first group that Leon had taken to Bombay. Joe Hayman was still there. The other changes were Brock in the place of Jack Butler and Benford in the place of Ted Fields.

Jimmy Monroe, who was the brother of Clark Monroe who had a famous club in Harlem, was in France because his wife Nina Mae McKinney who had starred in the first all-Negro movie produced in Hollywood "Halleluiah" was working in London, but Jimmy could not get permission to stay there and could only visit there for a few days at a time.

Jimmy opened a club in a small street called Cite Pigalle. Spider and his wife lived in this street and also Joe Hayman and wife. Bob Greir, another American Negro who had been in Paris for some time, was Jimmy's partner and the club, which I was told had never been a success for anyone that had ever tried to run it before, became a big success and meeting place for most Americans that were in Paris, and there were plenty of them.
